citation.sourceDocument: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration, no tax on earned wages (the Interest & Dividends Tax was repealed effective January 1, 2025)
citation.sourceNote: A state with no income tax is a first-class record here, not an omission: the shard exists, carries a citation, and answers "nothing" deliberately rather than by having nothing to say. The caveat that matters is what a $0 state income tax does NOT mean. A state still has to fund itself, and the ones without an income tax generally lean harder on sales and property taxes — neither of which this engine models. So a take-home figure here is exactly right about state income tax and silent about the rest of the state's tax burden; comparing two states on this number alone will mislead you. New Hampshire levies no tax on earned wages. It did tax interest and dividends, and that Interest & Dividends Tax was fully REPEALED effective January 1, 2025 — so a source describing New Hampshire as taxing investment income is describing a rule that no longer exists. New Hampshire has no sales tax and among the highest property taxes in the country, which is the trade this shard's $0 does not show.
